newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Coast Guard to safeguard oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Coast Guard to safeguard oil exports.

text.p: Venezuela's Coast Guard on Tuesday said they will arrest any fishermen attempting to block the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, used for 70 percent of the country's oil exports, and shippers expect business as usual on Thursday.
The fishermen's union Fetrapesca said 3,000 fishing boats will paralyse shipping in the channel on Thursday to highlight their plight after an oilspill on February 28.
"The position of the Venezuelan Navy and the Coast Guard is if the fishermen go into the channel, they are not allowed to block any ship," a coast guard official in Maracaibo said.
"If they block or attempt to block the shipping channel, they will be arrested," he added.
A shipping agent said he was chartering tankers to leave the Lake on Thursday and did not expect any disruption.
The fishermen are in a legal battle with the owners of the Nissos Amorgos tanker which ran aground in the channel on February 28, spilling 25,000 barrels of oil.

Intertanko, the international tanker owners association, said the fishermen filed a claim for $292.5 million against the owners, but the International Tanker Owners Pollution Fund (ITOPF) has called this an "insane number".

International treaties to which Venezuela is signatory provide compensation for lost earnings to all those affected by the spill up to about $82 million, of which $7.2 million is paid by the Nissos owner.
